communityVoices.quote: Scarlet in the first freaking set! Devil with a Blue Dress! Bertha>Greatest Story! On top of it, they played great! Bonus!
This playing recalls Fall 1984 it's so good. NFA is really hot, also the Scarlet near the beginning is really really tight and sounds like the very best of 1974 or 1976.
Jerry was really amazed by finally having a hit. It could have given him a boost, that might explain his wonderful performance, of course not only at this show, but during the whole year.
You can hear the crowd bum as this was pretty overused at this time and after hearing the first few bars you know they will just nail it and they did
Isn't it great that Jerry finally got the hit he'd always wanted?

whyThisShow: The setlist alone makes this one worth tracking down — Scarlet Begonias in the first set, a Rock 'n' Roll medley built around Devil With the Blue Dress, and Bertha into Greatest Story are not combinations you see every night. One listener noted this was one of those shows where "it wouldn't matter how they played, because they kicked down with such a fun, interesting and surprising setlist". Jerry in late 1987 was riding the momentum of a genuine pop hit, and one reviewer felt that "it could have given him a boost, that might explain his wonderful performance, of course not only at this show, but during the whole year". Brent and Bobby are not afterthoughts here — Stefan W. specifically noted that "Bobby is really putting all he's got into GSET and Throwing Stones, which is almost hypnotical".
listenFor: The Scarlet Begonias is a focal point for multiple reviewers — one called it "really really tight and sounds like the very best of 1974 or 1976". Worth noting that the crowd's initial reaction was skeptical, since capn doubledose remembered you "can hear the crowd bum as this was pretty overused at this time" before the band locked it in. The closing sequence draws particular attention — one reviewer warned that "if you don't almost cry during the very soft and emotional sung lines of Black Muddy River after an entirely perfect show, you can call me a liar". The NFA is also flagged as "really hot" by at least one listener.
context: This is a soundboard recording from the band's long residency run at Madison Square Garden in September 1987, sourced from the Hinko collection and marked sbeok (SBD okay). The show falls in the era immediately following Touch of Grey's chart run — it peaked at number 9 in 1987 — which brought an enormous new audience into MSG and gave the whole tour a charged atmosphere. The recording is unreleased officially, but the SBD source means the sound quality is well-documented by the community as strong, with one reviewer describing "a fine stage sound, which is simply amazing" alongside audible audience response.
funFact: One reviewer remembered showing up to the venue in a pinstriped suit after starting a new job, worried that "people would think I was a narc".
headline: MSG, September '87, setlist does the talking.
